ce_bugs.text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — Empty or missing destination calendars now dereference an undefined first item and abort event creation.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1077 — Collective host calendars are silently discarded when the organizer has no destination calendar because the member list is only appended to a non-null array.

mrv_findings.text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar") {` — failure mode: destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` can yield `undefined`, so strict TypeScript compilation rejects this unsafe property access. (confidence=75; severity=P1)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1877 — `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id },` — failure mode: persisting only the first collective host calendar causes confirmation and payment-delayed flows, which rebuild destinations from the booking, to omit every additional host calendar. (confidence=100; severity=P1)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),` — failure mode: this reverses organization-slug behavior under team billing, an unrelated product-policy change not traceable to the calendar destination-array conversion. (confidence=75; severity=P1)

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` — failure mode: when a collective organizer/event type has no destination calendar but a participating host does, the event starts as `null` and optional chaining discards every team calendar, so the new multi-host delivery path never creates those hosts’ events. (confidence=100; severity=P1)

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` — failure mode: EventManager iterates every selected destination but only Google matches the invocation credential; Lark (and the similarly changed Office365/CalDAV paths) always uses element zero, so multi-destination bookings write each credential’s event to the wrong calendar or fail for lack of access. (confidence=100; severity=P1)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:380 — `await Promise.all(destinationCalendarCredentials.map(async (c) => await createEvent(c, event)))` — failure mode: the no-credential branch drops `destination.externalId`, so Google falls back to `primary` and the persisted result has no external calendar id instead of the selected destination, breaking later update/delete routing. (confidence=100; severity=P1)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:208 — `externalCalendarId: result.externalId,` — failure mode: CalendarManager.updateEvent never returns `externalId` or `credentialId`, so edit-location creates new references with both routing fields unset and later operations fall back to arbitrary calendars. (confidence=100; severity=P1)

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — `const credentialFromDB = await prisma.credential.findUnique({` — failure mode: this per-destination query is awaited inside the new collective-calendar loop, creating serial N+1 credential fetches that make booking latency scale linearly with hosts. (confidence=100; severity=P2)
